title: Can a folded paper stack grow taller than the Burj Khalifa?
description: A stack of paper is about ten point four metres tall after twenty folds, and it is doubled fold after fold and compared with the Burj Khalifa and the Mariana Trench. Keeko's doubt is that ten more folds add only a little.
teaching_notes: One idea: each fold doubles the height, so the jumps keep getting bigger and the height soon passes tall buildings and deep trenches. Watch for students who think ten more folds add about the same amount as the first ten.

source: After 20 folds the stack is about 10.4 m. Find the thickness
video_script.why: The child can double a thickness fold by fold, and now sees the height pass a tall building and a deep trench.
video_script.substitution: The book's own stack, about ten point four metres after twenty folds, doubled on to thirty folds.
video_script.anchor: a stack of folded paper drawn beside the Burj Khalifa and the Mariana Trench
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks ten more folds add only half again to ten metres. Each fold doubles the height, so the height grows by far more.
video_script.payoff_line: After thirty folds, the stack is about ten point seven kilometres tall

final_answer.value: about 670 m, about 1.3 km and about 10.7 km
final_answer.spoken: about six hundred seventy metres, about one point three kilometres and about ten point seven kilometres

never_show: 15 m as the height after 30 folds, marked as right
maths_rules: after 20 folds about 10.4 m; about 21 m after 21 folds (10.4 × 2 = 20.8)
670 m < 830 m, the Burj Khalifa, so a little less
10.7 km is just short of 11 km, the depth of the Mariana Trench
slip: 10.4 + 10.4 ÷ 2 is about 15.6 m, adding instead of doubling
video_script.design: One idea: keep doubling and compare the height with a tower and a trench. The stack and the two landmarks stay all video; one slip at the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, double once more for twenty six folds, because each fold doubles the height.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Three hundred thirty six times two is six hundred seventy two.

<bookmark mark='compare'/>It is a little less than the Burj Khalifa.

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, the next fold doubles again.
Six hundred seventy two times two is one thousand three hundred forty four metres.
That is about one point three kilometres.
<bookmark mark='taller'/>That is taller than the Burj Khalifa.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 26 folds about 670 m; 27 folds about 1.3 km; 30 folds about 10.7 km, just short of 11 km

<bookmark mark='a27'/>After twenty seven folds, it is about one point three kilometres, above the tower.
<bookmark mark='a30'/>After thirty folds, the stack is about ten point seven kilometres tall.
That is a little short of the depth of the Mariana Trench.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks thirty folds give about fifteen metres, because ten more folds only add half again.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But each of those ten folds doubles the height, it does not add a little.
Ten doublings grow the stack by far more than half again.
